steps: Check the opening & chimney

Confirm the minimum opening (19-1/4" H, 29-1/2" front W, 15" D, 18-7/8" back W) and a 7" I.D. factory-built or 6" x 8" I.D. masonry chimney, 10'–50' tall. Measure base to chimney top, minus the insert height, for the flex-pipe length.

Installs only in a solid-fuel masonry or factory-built non-combustible fireplace built to code. Locate it out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies, on a level surface that can carry the insert and venting. It may be installed in a bedroom, and in an aftermarket, permanently located manufactured home (USA only) or mobile home where local codes allow.

  1. Remove and discard the existing chimney cap.
  2. With one person at the fireplace opening and one at the top of the chimney, measure from the fireplace base to the top of the chimney.
  3. Subtract the height of the insert. The result is the total length of co-linear flexible aluminum pipe needed (cut #816 to this length).

Smoke shelves, shields and baffles may be removed if mechanically fastened, and firebrick removed to reach the minimum opening. Cutting sheet metal parts of the existing fireplace is prohibited. If the metal floor is removed, set the insert directly on the metal base and attach the 'THIS UNIT HAS BEEN MODIFIED' label at the bottom of the existing firebox.

Where the chimney no longer terminates through the roof line, a co-linear to co-axial adapter may be fitted where it ends; the co-axial pipe then needs 1" clearance to combustibles on all sides.
Prepare the fireplace

Verify a clean, sound, non-combustible chimney; block the damper open or remove it, and remove the chimney cap. Plan the gas line (right side) and power, and attach the converted-fireplace warning label to the bottom of the existing firebox.

• Clean the chimney and fireplace to prevent a creosote odor entering the home. Verify combustible mantel and sidewall clearances (Section 8.0).
  • Refractory, glass doors, screen rails, screen mesh and log grates may be removed. Any removed parts must be capable of re-installation; removing rivets or screws is acceptable.
  • No gas access hole in a factory-built fireplace: one of 1½" (37.5mm) or less may be drilled through the lower sides or bottom of the firebox, then plugged with non-combustible insulation once the gas line is in.
  • Don't route the gas line where it would obstruct fan operation. At minimum opening dimensions the line may have to be run after the insert is placed.
  • Electrical outlet box location: Figure 2.1 (p. 9).

Label text: "This fireplace has been converted for use with a gas fireplace insert only and cannot be used for burning wood or solid fuels unless all original parts have been replaced, and the fireplace re-approved by the Authority Having Jurisdiction."
Assemble the vent & cap

Cut #816 to length and extend both pipes. The intake (end without collar) slides over cap collar A; the exhaust (red marking) gets sealant and goes onto collar B, with (3) self-tapping screws each and the exhaust collar on the right.

Proper operation requires the exhaust and combustion-air pipes on their correct collars at both the termination cap and the insert's vent adapter. The insert's exhaust collar is on the right side; install the cap with its exhaust collar on the right too.

  1. Measure the total chimney length and cut #816 (36' of 3" flexible pipe) to it.
  2. Carefully extend the exhaust and intake pipes to that length.
  3. Slide the intake pipe (end without a collar) over cap collar A and secure with (3) self-tapping screws (not provided).
  4. Run a bead of sealant around the inner edge of the exhaust pipe end, slide it onto collar B, secure with (3) self-tapping screws and seal around the joint.

Avoid tight bends that can abrade or damage the flexible pipe.

Note: the #816 drawing on p. 15 labels the sealant "(not provided)", but the vent-run and adapter steps on pp. 17 and 18 call for sealant "(provided)".
Run the vent down the chimney

Slide the vent adapter out of the channels on top of the insert, lower both 3" x 3" flex pipes down the chimney, and set the termination cap on a bead of sealant. Pull both pipes down into the firebox.

Complete everything in Section 5.0 first.

  • Through offsets, put a weighted rope around each pipe end to guide it. Don't tie one rope around both pipes.
  • To prevent cold air drafts, Hussong recommends insulating the flex pipes and chimney with unfaced insulation listed as noncombustible per ASTM E 136. Optional: wrap the first 3' (914mm) below the cap and secure with wire; optional: fill between the pipes and chimney to cut heat loss.
  • Set the cap on a liberal bead of sealant around the top of the chimney, per the vent manufacturer's instructions. #816-CAP option: 2" (50mm) self-tapping screws and anchor straps (not provided) through the pilot holes on the cap sides.
  • From inside the fireplace, pull the ropes or pipes down until both the exhaust and the combustion air intake are in the firebox.
Connect the vent & set the insert

Exhaust (red) goes inside the adapter's 'Exhaust' collar, intake over its collar, each with sealant and (3) ½" self-tapping screws. Slide the insert in, pull the adapter forward with the pull rod until seated, fix with (2) ½" sheet metal screws, and level.

1. Place the removed vent adapter into the fireplace opening.
  2. Exhaust pipe (red marking): bead of sealant, slide inside the collar marked 'Exhaust', (3) ½" (13mm) self-tapping screws, then more sealant for an airtight seal.
  3. Intake pipe: liberal bead of sealant on the intake collar, slide the pipe over it, (3) ½" (13mm) self-tapping screws, more sealant. Visually check both connections.
  4. Slide the insert in until the channels on top align with the adapter. Put the pull rod handle through the access slot at the top and hook it through the hole in the pull rod; push the insert in while pulling the adapter forward until seated.
  5. Secure the adapter through the top slots with (2) ½" (13mm) sheet metal screws (components packet). Use the pull rod handle to pull the adapter back to starting position, remove the handle and verify the vent connection.
  6. If needed, level with the leveling bolts threaded into the nuts at the bottom (2 each side).
Gas line connection

Qualified installer only (a licensed plumber or gas fitter in Massachusetts). Connect the listed ½" tee-handle manual shut-off and flexible connector to the ½" control valve inlet, preferably through the right-side hole and clear of the fan.

• Supplied: a 3/8" (10 mm) x 18" (457 mm) long flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve. If substituting these components, check local codes.
  • Run the line to the point where the shut-off valve and flexible line connect. At minimum opening dimensions it may have to be run after the insert is placed.
  • Supply-system pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At or below ½ psi: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Follow local building codes, or ANSI Z223.1 where there are none. High altitude: consult the local gas distributor or the authority having jurisdiction for rating methods.
  • Check all connections, field or factory made, for leaks with soapy water (p. 29).
Shroud & safety barrier

Lift out the upper and lower louvers and the glass, fix the shroud to the cabinet's mounting nuts with (4) truss head screws, and refit the parts. Hang the barrier's tabs in the (4) shroud slots; trim must not seal the existing fireplace's ventilation or draft-relief openings.

The flow of combustion and ventilation air must not be obstructed.

The barrier provided must be installed. It fits properly only when the bottom of the fireplace is level with the finished hearth, so allow for the hearth finish when building a platform. To remove it, lift it up and out of the slots.

For the low mantel clearances, fit the CK29-LMK heat deflector to a CK29-RSF or CK29-PSF screen front; its gasket must contact the shroud (pp. 24–25). Outdoors, black painted barriers are recommended; plated or patina finishes oxidize and discolor.
Light kit, media & logs

Fit the (4) halogen bulbs without bare hands, add the crushed glass media and lava rock in front of the burner, then seat the CK29-50B logs on the burner pins and notches. Keep logs off the burner ports and brush on the rockwool embers.

Convert to propane, if needed, before the light kit or log set. Disconnect all electrical power before the light kit.

  1. Remove the barrier, glass, logs and refractory panels, the burner assembly ((2) screws), the ember panel and the burner ((2) screws at the back corners).
  2. Install the (4) halogen bulbs (components packet) in the lamp bases, handling them with a soft cloth. Refit the ember panel, burner and burner assembly.
  3. Place the crushed glass media in the ember media cavity in front of the burner assembly; scatter the lava rock on top.
  4. Logs (log set CK29-50B, numbered on the bottom): ember panel in front of the burner; CK29-1A, CK29-2A, CK29-3A and CK29-4 pushed down onto the burner mounting pins; CK29-5 and CK29-8 aligned with the notches on the base logs; CK29-6 and CK29-7 positioned as shown in the drawings on p. 28.
  5. Distribute the rockwool embers onto the logs and burner with a stiff bristle brush.
Don't place logs directly over burner port holes: it can affect flame appearance and build soot on the glass.
The troubleshooting chart on p. 40 prints the log set as #CK29-500; the parts list (p. 43) and pp. 5 and 28 give CK29-50B.
Initialize the controls

Clear all packaging from the firebox; rocker switch OFF, (4) AA in the backup holder, (3) AAA in the remote, then plug in. Press red SW1 (3 beeps), then remote ON/OFF within 5 seconds (4 beeps, pilot lights), ON/OFF again, then rocker ON.

Initializing starts pilot start-up in manual mode: the igniter sparks repeatedly and the pilot lights if gas is supplied.

  1. Press the red SW1 button on the IFC module: it beeps (3) times and lights an amber LED, ready to synchronize.
  2. Within (5) seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: (4) beeps, the transmitter code is accepted and the pilot lights.
  3. Press ON/OFF again: the pilot goes out, confirming the command.
  4. Set the main ON/OFF rocker switch to ON for remote operation.

Pilot mode: with the system OFF, press the mode key to the CPI icon, then the up arrow for CPI or the down arrow for IPI (single beep). In CPI the pilot turns off after 7 consecutive days without main burner ignition.

Manual operation without the remote: rocker OFF, press SW1 until (3) beeps and the amber LED, then press SW1 again within (5) seconds. The pilot lights, and the rocker switch then runs the main burner on HI only.
Pressure test & flame check

Check inlet (tap A) and manifold (tap B) pressures, then retighten each tap and confirm it is sealed. The venturi is factory set (NG 3/16", LP 5/8" open); flames start blue and should turn yellow during the first 15 minutes.

Venturi adjustment must be done by a qualified service technician. Let the fireplace cool, remove the barrier, glass, log set and burner assembly, loosen the venturi screw, adjust, retighten and refit. Slight changes give dramatic results: burn at least 15 minutes and let it cool between adjustments. If there is soot on the glass, check log positioning first.

Dark orange, black tipsventuri closed too far: open slightly
Short, blue flamesventuri open too far: close slightly
Lifting (ghosting) flamesgas pressure too high (check manometer) or venturi closed too far (open slightly)
Factory venturi openingNG 3/16" (4.8 mm) · LP 5/8" (16 mm)

Annual check (p. 42): the main burner must light within (4) seconds of the main gas valve opening, and the flame safety system must de-energize the safety shutoff in no more than (30) seconds.

Note: p. 38 says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner (and to close it slightly for short, blue flames), but the troubleshooting chart on p. 40 says to open the air shutter slightly when the flame burns blue and lifts off the burner.

panels.title: Pilot won't light or stay lit
items: Power interrupted → restore power, or run on fully charged battery back-up
Wiring disconnected → check every connection against the wiring schematic
Gas off, no propane or low pressure (bent line, narrow pipe, low line pressure) → check all shut-offs; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot flame not touching the rectification sensor → adjust the valve's pilot screw (clockwise decreases, counterclockwise increases), then reseal it

panels.title: Burner won't light / no response
items: Rocker switch OFF → set it to ON
Gas off or low, plugged main burner orifice, wiring fault, or pilot flame not directed onto the burner
No call for heat → remote powered ON, thermostat operation OFF
No reaction to commands → replace batteries, reprogram the remote to the IFC module, or reset the IFC after too many failed ignitions

panels.title: Pilot & burner go out while running
items: Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked; improper horizontal pitch; exhaust leaking back into the firebox
Excessive draft → a restrictor may need to be installed or modified

panels.title: Soot, blue or lifting flames
items: Soot on glass → log and media placement (p. 28), venturi air shutter may need opening slightly, vent cap installation or blockage
Flame blue and lifting off burner → venturi setting, vent cap installation, vent blockage or leak
Venturi for blue flames: p. 38 says to close the setting slightly for short, blue flames; the p. 40 chart says to open the air shutter slightly when the flame burns blue and lifts off the burner

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace has an ignition device that lights the pilot for you. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Everyday start

  1. Check that the main ON/OFF rocker switch is ON. It must be on for the remote to work.
  2. Press the ON/OFF key on the remote. The control module beeps once.
  3. About 4 seconds later it starts sparking at the pilot. Once the pilot lights, it lights the burner.

If the pilot doesn't light within 60 seconds, the module waits about 35 seconds and tries once more. If that fails too, see "Won't light?"

The full lighting procedure

  1. Read the safety information first.
  2. Press OFF on the remote and turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  3. Find the manual gas valve your service technician installed. Turn it clockwise to OFF.
  4. Wait 5 minutes for any gas to clear. Then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  5. Turn the valve counterclockwise to ON.
  6. Turn the power back on and press ON on the remote.
Turn the valve by hand only, never with tools. If it won't turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion. If the fireplace still won't operate, shut off its gas and call your service technician or gas supplier.

remote.title: Using the Proflame 2 remote
remote.html:
The remote runs on 3 AAA batteries. Most features are reached with the Mode key, then the up and down arrows. A single beep from the fireplace confirms a command.

  • ON/OFF key: turns the fireplace on and off.
  • Flame height: there are 6 flame levels. The down arrow lowers the flame one level at a time, all the way to off. The up arrow raises it. If the system is on but the flame is off, the up arrow relights it on HI.
  • Thermostat: press the thermostat key, then set the room temperature you want with the arrows. Keep pressing until SMART appears and the flame turns down by itself as the room reaches that temperature. In smart mode you can't adjust the flame by hand.
  • Fan (optional): press Mode to the fan icon and use the arrows. It has 6 speeds. In thermostat mode the fan waits 5 minutes after the fire lights and runs about 12 minutes after it turns off. In manual mode it runs at its last setting with no delay.
  • Accent light (if fitted): press Mode to the light icon. It has 6 brightness levels.
  • Key lock: press Mode and the up arrow together. A lock icon shows while it's on.
  • °F or °C: with the system off, press the thermostat key and Mode together.
A battery icon on the screen means the remote batteries are low. Replace them and the icon goes away.

firstfire.title: First fires: what's normal
firstfire.html:
Foggy glass

When the fireplace is first lit, condensation appears on the glass. This is normal in all gas fireplaces and disappears after several minutes.

A paint smell

You'll notice a paint smell during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off for this period. It helps the paint cure faster.

Ticks and creaks

Metal expands and contracts as it heats and cools, so the fireplace can make noises. That's normal and doesn't affect how well it works or how long it lasts.

Blue flames at first

When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn to the yellow you want: lazy, yellow flames. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips and soot, have a qualified service technician check the burner's air setting.

A short pause

When the pilot has been lit continuously, the system turns itself off for about 5 seconds within 24 hours to run a safety check. Then it carries out your last command again.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is a homeowner job, once a year. Only do it when the fireplace is completely cool. Never clean hot glass.

  1. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. Pull the 2 spring-loaded latches at the bottom of the firebox out and down. Lift the glass assembly up and off the 2 tabs at the top.
  4. Clean the glass with a suitable fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. To refit, hook the slots at the top of the glass over the tabs, lower the bottom into place, then pull the latches out and up to lock it.
  6. Put the safety screen back. Never run the fireplace without it.
Don't strike or slam the glass. Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken. Replacing it is a job for a qualified service person, and Hussong supplies the glass only as a complete assembly.
Soot on the glass? It can come from logs sitting over the burner ports, the burner's air setting, or a vent cap problem. Have a qualified technician check it.

off.title: Turning it off
off.html:
Everyday

Press the ON/OFF key on the remote. The control module beeps once, the screen shows only the room temperature, and the burner goes out.

Shut off the gas

Do this if the fireplace won't operate, or before service:

  1. Press OFF on the remote.
  2. If service is planned, turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  3. Find the manual valve your service technician installed and turn it clockwise to OFF.

Why is the pilot still lit?

The pilot has two modes. In IPI mode the system sparks to light the pilot each time. In CPI (continuous pilot) mode the pilot stays lit even when the burner is off. That keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the burner lights with less disruption to the air flow. A snowflake icon on the remote means CPI is on.

To switch, turn the system off, press Mode until the CPI icon shows, then press the up arrow for CPI or the down arrow for IPI. One beep confirms.

In CPI mode, if the burner doesn't light for 7 consecutive days, the pilot turns off on its own as a safety feature. Each time the burner lights, the 7-day timer starts over.

power.title: Power & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace plugs into a grounded three-prong outlet (120V) that must be powered at all times. It shouldn't be on a switch. Never cut or remove the plug's grounding prong.

Backup pack on the control module4 × AA (not included)
Remote3 × AAA (included)

In a power outage

The fireplace runs on the backup battery pack, but only the burner works. The fan and light won't run on battery power. How long the batteries last depends on their quality and how many times the fireplace lights.

Low-battery signs

  • Backup pack: the control module double-beeps when it gets an ON/OFF command, and its red light blinks once at intervals. Replace the AA batteries. It won't accept commands until you do, and it beeps once when the new batteries power it.
  • Remote: a battery icon appears on its screen before the batteries die. It disappears once you replace them.

wontlight.title: If it won't light
wontlight.html:
When you press ON, the control module sparks at the pilot for up to 60 seconds. If the pilot doesn't light, it pauses about 35 seconds and sparks for another 60 seconds. If that fails too, it locks out, and its red light blinks 3 times at intervals until you reset it.

Reset after a lockout

  • Press ON/OFF on the remote to turn it off, wait about 2 seconds, and press it again; or
  • Set the ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF, wait about 2 seconds, and set it back to ON.

The ignition sequence then starts again.

Simple checks

  • Is the gas on? There may be more than one shut-off valve between the fireplace and the main gas line.
  • Is the rocker switch ON? Is the remote on, with its thermostat turned off?
  • Are the remote and backup batteries fresh?
  • On propane, is there propane in the tank?

Red light blink codes

1 blinkbackup batteries low: replace them
2 blinkspilot flame error: contact your dealer
3 blinkslockout: reset as above
The full troubleshooting chart is for a qualified technician.

safety.title: Safety around the fireplace
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building immediately.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before lighting, smell around the fireplace for gas, including next to the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles there.

Hot glass and children

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the safety barrier in place. If it gets damaged, replace it with Hussong's barrier for this fireplace.
  • Supervise young children in the same room. If someone at risk lives in the house, a physical barrier such as an adjustable safety gate is recommended.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from the fireplace. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids nearby.
  • Never burn wood, coal, paper or cardboard in it.
  • Don't use it if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have the fireplace inspected before use and at least once a year by a professional service person. If there's a lot of lint from carpeting or bedding, it may need cleaning more often.

Fanevery 6 months
Firebox and bottom latchesannually
Vent systemannually
Burner and pilotannually
Glass inspectionannually

The technician vacuums the fan (its bearings are sealed and need no oil), the firebox and the burner system, checks gas connections for leaks, checks the pilot and the flame safety system, and examines the vent system. Burner flames should be steady, not lifting or floating.

Cleaning the glass once a year is your job. See "Clean the glass."

Keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that can burn, and of gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.

warranty.title: Limited lifetime warranty
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. warrants the fireplace to the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, against defects in materials and workmanship. You don't need to send anything in to register. Keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model.

30 days · parts & laborpaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts & laborall other parts and material, subject to the exclusions
Years 2 through lifetime · parts onlyfirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front viewing glass (thermal shock only), refractory firebox liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed to an authorized dealer only. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids or limits it

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not installed, operated and maintained per the manual.
  • Serial number or testing label removed, or the fireplace altered or tampered with.
  • Submersion in water, or long periods of dampness or condensation.
  • Installation problems such as inadequate venting, excessive offsets or negative air pressure; chimney parts and non-Hussong accessories.
The warranty can't be transferred. This is a summary; the full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5" WC min – 10.5" WC max · 7" WC recommended
Propane12" WC min – 13" WC max
Propane recommended12" WC (2.99 kPa) (Table 7.1)

Test at the valve's IN tap (A) with a manometer on a ¼ in (6 mm) I.D. hose, with the pilot and burner lit and all other gas appliances in the house on or at full capacity. If the reading is too high or too low, contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming pressure. After tightening the tap (snug, not over-tight), relight and reattach the manometer: it should read no pressure.

Disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve from the supply piping for tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa); at or below ½ psi, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas low / high1.1" / 3.8" WC
Propane low / high2.9" / 11" WC

Measure at the valve's OUT tap (B): light the pilot, loosen the tap screw counter-clockwise, attach the manometer (¼ in (6 mm) I.D. hose), light the burner and read. Turn burner and pilot off, disconnect, and tighten the screw snug (don't over-tighten). Reattach the manometer to confirm the tap is sealed: no pressure with pilot and burner on.

Gas pressure too high can cause lifting (ghosting) flames.

9" (229mm) mantel, above top of appliance16" (407mm)
6" mantel with CK29-LMK, above top11"
Maker's website: its brochure lists mantel 9" deep: 16" from top of insert (11" with Low Mantel Kit). Install to the manual.

From the starting mantel, projections can increase 1" of depth for every 1" of height. The low mantel figures apply only with the CK29-LMK installed, and the kit is for use only with the CK29-RSF and CK29-PSF safety barriers. Figure 8.2 notes that a combustible floor can be in front of and underneath the unit. Trim panels or surrounds must not seal the existing fireplace's ventilation openings or block draft relief openings.

Outdoor covered installation

Allowed where the fireplace is protected from direct precipitation. Operation is approved from 40°F to 110°F. The overhang in front, and to each side, must be at least 1/2 the roofline elevation above the base of the fireplace. Wiring must meet the outdoor requirements of NFPA 70.

The manual also prints the 55" ceiling clearance as (1.04m) and the 16" mantel height as (254mm) on p. 22, and the 9" mantel as (254mm) on p. 23; it gives 55" (1.40m) on pp. 23 and 25, 16" (407mm) on p. 23 and 9" (229mm) on p. 22.

The AC supply must be hot at all times, with no switch in it. Plug into a properly grounded three-prong receptacle and ground per local codes, or ANSI/NFPA 70 or CSA C22.1. Fan and light don't run on battery back-up. Shut off the household breaker before working on electrical lines. Electrical access location: Figure 2.1, p. 9.

review.notes: Manual gives no efficiency, heating area, emissions or viewing area, so the catalog AFUE figures and view_area are unverified. Figure-only content not transcribed: appliance dimensions (p. 9), safety barrier sizes (p. 11), mantel drawings (pp. 23, 25), low mantel kit assembly (p. 24), final log positions (p. 28), flame appearance photos (pp. 38, 42). Table 7.1 (p. 21) prints a stray 'recommended' under the propane row with no value attached; propane shown as 12"-13" WC per Table 12.1 (p. 37). Section 11.9.5 'Turn OFF' (p. 35) repeats the turn-on wording ('to turn ON the appliance'); the guide says press ON/OFF to turn off, as the rest of that section describes. Fan: remote section is headed 'Fan Speed Control (optional)' (p. 36) while Table 2.1 (p. 10) lists the fan kit as a field-assembled part; catalog says blower standard, not listed as a mismatch. Catalog feature 'one-piece shroud required' vs parts list (p. 43), which also lists 4-piece blank shrouds CK29-004 / CK29-008. Minor metric rounding not flagged (24" = 609 vs 610mm; 10' = 3.05 vs 3m). Massachusetts sidewall-vent rules (p. 7) omitted as this insert vents up the chimney. Pages 2, 4, 6 and 45 have no extracted text (blank in the source).
